differences: The paper reports 19857 analysed epochs (13377 opposing, 6480 following); these counts are reproduced only by the file as shared, which still holds the five participants whose data the authors drop before the statistics. After dropping them the file has 18401 classified epochs.

Epochs discarded per participant: the paper reports a mean of 77.3 (10.7% of 720), a maximum of 264 and four participants above 200; the shared file gives 100.9 (14.0%), 399 and seven over all 49 participants, and 88.1, 325 and five over the 44 kept. Not used as checks.
The largest number of epochs behind a non-null contour is 41 in the shared file; the paper states a maximum of 40 (ranging from 20).
peaks.csv holds 42 participants and 15 contours each (630 rows), not the 44 participants and 656 contours described in the paper; the epoch file reproduces the 656.
